guard: DECLARED SURVIVOR of `npm run verify` (limitation L6). Settlement is two-stage; stage 2's half-EVEN mode is witnessed by 274 exact 8-dp ties in the capture and is killed by the half-up mutation in tests/mutations.json. Stage 1's mode is NOT witnessed. Exact 8-dp ties in 9900/basisPoints exist at only two basis points, 2048 (multiplier 4.833984375) and 6144 (1.611328125) — and only 6144 DISCRIMINATES: at 2048 the quotient before the tie digit is odd, so half-up and half-even both resolve to 4.83398438 and the two modes agree. At 6144 half-up gives 1.61132813 and half-even 1.61132812, and even there the difference survives only at a stake that preserves it — $1 does, $0.10 erases it in the stage-2 rounding. So the single discriminating case is a settled win on basisPoints 6144 at a stake of $1 or more. No captured bet lands on either band, so switching stage 1 to half-even changes no credit in the dataset and no scored step can see it. The audit models stage 1 as half-up (Math.round) and states that as an ASSUMED premise rather than a finding; the shipped 9,800-case sweep in tests/dice/settlementTests.ts compares Math.round against exact half-up, so it is tie-safe by its own definition and would pass under either operator mode. Only a live capture can produce the discriminating evidence.
